explanation: %s reads characters until whitespace with no width limit, so a 30-character word writes past the end of the 16-byte buffer — a classic stack buffer overflow. The fix is a width-bounded conversion (%15s) or fgets with an explicit size.
prompt: A user types a 30-character word. What's the bug?
choices: %s reads unbounded input, so a long word overflows the 16-byte buffer — use %15s or fgets
